pr_title: Initialise variables to avoid linking issues
pr_body:
With legacy toolchains, uninitialised variables cause issues such as duplicate symbols when it comes to linking.

Fixes #23540
Perhaps also fixes #23528 

CLA: trivial
pr_comments:
Initialisation of global variables has never been explicitly required - they were always put into BSS and initialised to 0 by the run time.

As far back as the C89 standard:

> If an object that has static storage duration is not initialized explicitly, it is initialized implicitly as if every member that has arithmetic type were assigned 0 and every member that has pointer type were assigned a null pointer constant.

It really seems that there is some other problem with these legacy toolchains, and that this inadvertently fixes it

(NOTE: "static storage duration" includes anything declared at file scope, not just with `static`)

issue_context.title: Symbol issues when linking libcrypto.3.dylib on the Intel build of OS X 10.4 (darwin 8)
issue_context.body:
When building on OS X 10.4 (intel), the build fails with the following error.
```
ld: common symbols not allowed with MH_DYLIB output format with the -multi_module option
crypto/bio/libcrypto-shlib-bio_addr.o definition of common _bio_lookup_lock (size 16)
crypto/bio/libcrypto-shlib-bio_meth.o definition of common _bio_type_count (size 16)
crypto/engine/libcrypto-shlib-eng_lib.o definition of common _global_engine_lock (size 16)
crypto/libcrypto-shlib-cpuid.o definition of common _OPENSSL_ia32cap_P (size 16)
/usr/libexec/gcc/i686-apple-darwin8/4.0.1/libtool: internal link edit command failed
```
To sidestep the issue, adding `-fno-common` to `CFLAGS` allows the build to complete.
It seems the issue is not specific to building on intel darwin as there is a report with duplicate symbols on 32bit intel build of Fedora #23528
